summary: The Kidney Disease Education Access Expansion Act of 2026 amends the Social Security Act and the Public Health Service Act to expand Medicare and private health insurance coverage for kidney disease education services, screenings, and related care beginning January 1, 2027.

affected_groups.effect: Gain broader access to kidney disease education services, group sessions, caregiver participation, telehealth options, and screenings during annual and initial wellness visits.
Gain coverage for kidney disease education services as a preventive service starting in plan years on or after January 1, 2027.
Includes a wider array of medical professionals and trained community health workers who are qualified to furnish and be paid for kidney disease education services.
affected_groups.group: Health care providers and qualified personnel

key_provisions: Expands the definition of qualified persons who can provide kidney disease education services to include physician assistants, nurses, clinical social workers, registered dietitians, and trained community health workers.

Expands patient eligibility for kidney disease education services from only stage IV chronic kidney disease to individuals with hypertension, diabetes, any stage of chronic kidney disease, or other risk factors.
Permits group education sessions, the presence of caregivers, and broadens the scope of education topics such as therapeutic options, post-transplant support, and transition assistance.
Adds chronic kidney disease screenings and education services to Medicare initial preventive physical examinations and annual wellness visits.
Revises session limits to a number determined appropriate by the Secretary in consultation with stakeholders, and allows delivery through telehealth.
Establishes a Kidney Disease Education Effectiveness Working Group to develop evaluation methodologies and a comprehensive assessment framework.
Requires private health insurance plans to cover kidney disease education services as preventive services without cost-sharing.
missing_information: Specific budget scores or total cost estimates for implementing the expanded Medicare and private insurance requirements.
The exact number of kidney disease education sessions the Secretary will ultimately determine as appropriate beyond the prior limit of six sessions.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Kidney Disease Education Access Expansion Act of 2026 amends the Social Security Act and the Public Health Service Act to expand Medicare and private health insurance coverage for kidney disease education services, screenings, and related care beginning January 1, 2027.
summary_detail.significance: The bill broadens preventive healthcare access and educational resources for individuals with or at risk for kidney disease across both Medicare and private insurance programs, while establishing formal working groups to evaluate patient outcomes.

title: Kidney Disease Education Access Expansion Act of 2026
